title: Prepare wavefunk-ui for first project integrations
description: Make wavefunk-ui ready to use as the common Askama + htmx UI base for new Wave Funk Rust projects. The crate must stay publishable, ship self-contained CSS/fonts/JS, support fast local iteration through gitignored consumer path overrides, and provide enough typed components, docs, and browser QA to unblock a separate first-consumer integration epic.
close_reason: All integration readiness child tasks are closed; release, package, browser QA, component API, assets, and Woodpecker workflows are verified

title: Stabilize the public component API contract
description: Define the public API rules for typed Askama components: naming, builder patterns, htmx attrs, HTML escaping and trusted slots, error handling, feature flags, and semver expectations. Acceptance: README and AGENTS document the contract; component constructors follow one consistent pattern; examples show safe attrs and safe inner HTML slots.
notes: Askama integration research: prefer exported Rust component types plus HtmlSafe over asking consumer crates to import template macro files from this crate. Askama macro/import/include paths are resolved at the deriving crate's compile time through that crate's template dirs, so dependency-crate macro files are awkward for crates.io consumers. Useful supported patterns: templates-in-templates with nested Template values; implement askama::filters::HtmlSafe for wavefunk component types so consumers can render {{ component }} without |safe; use call-block macros only inside this crate's own templates/gallery; expose public helper functions/newtypes for safe asset links and htmx attributes; use block/blocks for internal partials, not as the cross-crate API.
close_reason: Done: component API contract documented and backed by builders, htmx attr helpers, TrustedHtml slots, tests, and gallery examples.

title: Harden embedded asset distribution
description: Make the embedded asset API production-ready for self-contained binaries. Cover CSS/fonts/wavefunk.js/htmx/SSE, content types, cache policy, optional Axum router, framework-neutral lookup, license notes, and a stable default mount path. Acceptance: cargo package includes every asset; tests cover key assets and path rejection; docs show how consumers mount assets without runtime static directories.
close_reason: Done: embedded assets cover CSS/fonts/Wave Funk JS/htmx/SSE with constants, content types, cache policy, path normalization, package verification, and docs.

title: Port action and form primitives
description: Add typed Askama wrappers for the components most projects need immediately: icon button, button group, split button, input, textarea, select, input group, checkbox/radio row, switch, range, and form field variants. Acceptance: each wrapper renders Wave Funk markup, supports htmx attrs where relevant, has tests for escaping/classes, and appears in the gallery.
close_reason: Done: action and form wrappers added with tests for classes, escaping, htmx attrs, and gallery coverage.

title: Port layout, navigation, and data-display primitives
description: Add typed Askama wrappers for app shell variants, panel, card, table, definition list, stat, badge, avatar, breadcrumbs, tabs, segmented control, pagination, sidebar/topbar helpers, statusbar, empty state, and basic grid/split layout. Acceptance: wrappers cover the common app-page patterns needed by Sendword-style projects and render in the gallery.
close_reason: Done: layout, navigation, data-display, app-shell variant helpers, tests, and gallery coverage added.

title: Port feedback, overlay, and htmx interaction primitives
description: Add wrappers and JS conventions for modal, drawer, popover/menu, toast, echo/minibuffer, tooltip, skeleton, spinner, alert/callout variants, and htmx response helper functions. Acceptance: header-triggered toasts/echo work in browser QA; modal/popover/drawer behavior is documented; no consumer-specific JS leaks into the shared crate.
close_reason: Done: feedback/overlay/loading wrappers, htmx trigger header helpers, documented interaction conventions, gallery coverage, and browser-verified toast/echo headers.

title: Validate Askama performance and local rebuild ergonomics
description: Apply Askama performance guidance to this crate and consumer usage. Acceptance: docs tell consumers to use render/render_into/write_into instead of to_string/format for templates; dev profile optimizes askama_derive; local path override rebuild times are checked with a template-heavy example; identify any types that should implement FastWritable.
close_reason: Implemented FastWritable guidance, local rebuild check, and docs

title: Build a complete gallery and browser QA surface
description: Turn the current Axum example into the integration readiness gallery. It should render every public component, exercise embedded assets, htmx interactions, light/dark mode, dense/default density, and responsive app-shell behavior. Acceptance: agent-browser smoke checks cover page load, asset requests, toasts/echo, and representative interactions with no console errors.
close_reason: Gallery covers public components, variants, assets, htmx toast/echo, popover, and responsive shell; agent-browser smoke passed with no console errors

title: Prove integration in one real Wave Funk consumer
description: Integrate wavefunk-ui into one existing Wave Funk Rust app using a gitignored .cargo/config.toml path override for local iteration while keeping the committed manifest on the crates.io dependency. Acceptance: the consumer mounts embedded assets, renders at least one shared layout and several shared components, builds as a self-contained binary, and verifies release/CI would resolve crates.io without the local override.

title: Finish crates.io and release readiness
description: Prepare the crate for the first published release after the core readiness work is complete. Acceptance: README examples are accurate, include list is complete, license/third-party notices are present, cargo package and cargo publish --dry-run pass, versioning/release notes are defined, and any CI/release workflow is in place.
close_reason: Added Woodpecker CI and tag release pipelines, release docs, release notes, package notices, and publish dry-run preflight

title: Epic: fill missing typed UI component coverage
description:
Current state: wavefunk-ui already exposes typed primitives for buttons, field/input/textarea/select/check/switch/range, simple Table, layout primitives, overlays, feedback, and gallery coverage.

Gap: several useful app components are either CSS-only in static/wavefunk/css/04-components.css or absent as higher-level Askama APIs. Consumers should not need to copy raw class markup for common forms, tables, progress, stepper, data-display, and identity patterns.

Goal: add focused, publishable typed Askama component APIs using Type::new constructors, named variant constructors, by-value with_* builders, HtmlAttr for htmx attributes, TrustedHtml for explicit markup slots, gallery examples, render tests, and the normal release verification path.

title: Add typed form composition components
description:
Current state: Field, Input, Textarea, Select, InputGroup, CheckRow, Switch, and Range exist, but consumers still need to hand-compose full forms, sections, fieldsets, and action rows.

Implement typed Askama APIs for common form composition: Form, FormSection or Fieldset, FormRow where useful, and FormActions. Preserve framework neutrality and expose method/action/enctype plus HtmlAttr passthrough for htmx. Slots that contain controls or buttons must use TrustedHtml.

Acceptance: add templates and constructors/builders, include a realistic form in examples/axum_gallery.rs, add render tests for escaped labels/attrs and trusted slots, and keep just fmt/test/clippy plus cargo package passing.

title: Expand table API for real data workflows
description:
Current state: Table, TableHeader, TableRow, and TableCell cover simple escaped-text tables. CSS already includes wf-tablewrap, wf-filterbar, wf-bulkbar, wf-tablescroll, wf-tablefoot, wf-sort-h, sort arrows, column width helpers, sticky headers, and pinned last columns.

Implement typed APIs for the missing table workflow layer: TableWrap/TableChrome, filter toolbar slot, bulk action bar, footer slot, sortable headers, width/alignment helpers, and a safe path for action or rich cells using TrustedHtml without weakening escaped text defaults.

Acceptance: simple Table remains source compatible; new constructors/builders follow the component API contract; gallery demonstrates search/filter, sort header, selected rows, bulk actions, and pinned actions; render tests cover escaping, selected state, sort state, and trusted action cells.

title: Add dropzone and file input components
description:
Current state: generic Input can render type=file via with_type, and CSS already defines wf-dropzone, wf-dropzone-input, wf-dropzone-frame, dragover, and disabled states. There is no typed Dropzone/FileInput component or gallery coverage.

Implement a typed Dropzone component for file intake with name, title, hint, accept, multiple, disabled, dragover/open-state class, and HtmlAttr passthrough. Consider a lightweight FileInput named constructor if it reduces consumer boilerplate without duplicating Dropzone.

Acceptance: normal labels and hints are escaped, attrs are escaped, multiple/accept/disabled render correctly, gallery includes the upload pattern, and tests cover the safe markup contract.

title: Add progress, meter, and keyboard hint primitives
description:
Current state: CSS includes wf-progress, wf-progress-fill, indeterminate progress, wf-meter, wf-meter-fill, and wf-kbd. Spinner and Skeleton have typed APIs, and MenuItem can render inline kbd text, but there is no standalone Progress, Meter, or Kbd component.

Implement typed Progress, Meter, and Kbd components. Progress should support determinate percentage and indeterminate mode. Meter should expose value/width/height/color through safe style variables or bounded builders. Kbd should render escaped key labels for standalone shortcuts and menu hints.

Acceptance: gallery demonstrates each primitive, render tests cover determinate/indeterminate classes and escaping, and API avoids arbitrary unsafe style injection except through deliberate attrs where already allowed.

title: Add stepper and wizard progress components
description:
Current state: CSS includes wf-stepper, wf-step, wf-step-num, is-active, and is-done states, but there is no typed Stepper API or template.

Implement Stepper and StepItem structs for multi-step flows. Support numbered steps, active/done/upcoming states, optional href for navigable steps, aria-current on the active step, and attrs where useful. Keep it server-rendered and framework-neutral.

Acceptance: add template, constructors/builders, gallery example, tests for state classes/aria-current/escaping, and do not require JavaScript.

title: Add accordion and FAQ components
description:
Current state: CSS includes wf-accordion/wf-accordion-item/wf-accordion-trigger/wf-accordion-body and wf-faq rows, but consumers have no typed Accordion or FAQ APIs.

Implement server-rendered Accordion, AccordionItem, Faq, and FaqItem components. Use details/summary for accordion behavior, support open state, and use TrustedHtml only for answer/body slots that may contain markup. Plain questions/titles should be escaped strings.

Acceptance: gallery demonstrates both accordion and FAQ variants, tests cover open state, escaped question text, trusted answer slot rendering, and no JavaScript dependency is introduced.

title: Add identity and brand chrome components
description:
Current state: Avatar exists, CSS includes wf-avatar-group, wf-user, compact user variants, wf-mark, and wf-wordmark, but there are no typed AvatarGroup, UserButton/UserProfileMenu trigger, or Wordmark components.

Implement typed components for identity and brand chrome: AvatarGroup, UserButton or UserProfile, and Wordmark/BrandMark wrapper. Integrate with existing Avatar and Popover/Menu patterns without duplicating behavior.

Acceptance: gallery shows sidebar-style and compact topbar identity controls, avatar groups, and a wordmark; tests cover escaped names/emails, compact/full classes, image alt behavior, and optional TrustedHtml mark slot.

title: Add operational data display components
description:
Current state: CSS includes wf-rank, wf-feed, wf-timeline, wf-tree, and wf-framed, but none are exposed as typed Askama components. Existing data-display coverage stops at StatRow, Table, DefinitionList, Grid, Split, and EmptyState.

Implement typed components for dashboard and operational displays: RankList/RankRow, Feed/FeedRow, Timeline/TimelineItem, TreeView/TreeItem, and Framed/CodeFrame where appropriate. Keep text escaped by default and require TrustedHtml only for rich bodies.

Acceptance: add templates, builders, gallery examples with realistic dashboard data, and tests for active/collapsed states, escaping, and percentage/width handling for rank bars.

title: Decide and expose marketing page primitives
description:
Current state: static/wavefunk/css/06-marketing.css defines mk-wrap, nav, hero, sections, feature grid, steps, code block, showcase, footer, and colophon classes. Some pricing/testimonial CSS also lives in 04-components.css. None of these have typed Askama APIs.

Audit whether marketing primitives belong in the public component API or should remain CSS-only. If they belong, implement typed components for the stable low-risk pieces first, such as MarketingWrap, MarketingSection, FeatureGrid, StepGrid, MarketingFooter, PricingPlans, and Testimonial.

Acceptance: document the decision in README or task comments, add typed APIs only for stable patterns, include gallery or example coverage, and avoid locking app-specific landing-page copy/layout into semver-sensitive structs.
